title: Production Readiness Report (S9 output, human gate artifact)
description: Machine-readable half of the S9 gate report. Answers one question: can this move forward safely, and under what conditions? Short, specific, decision-ready — evidence a release reviewer, support owner, or customer team needs, not an inventory of every operational detail.

deployment_context.description: Q1: What are we deploying, and where will it run?

intended_users.description: Who or what will call this (users, systems, service accounts)

environment.description: Environment under review and exposure level; staging/production separation noted

environment_provenance.description: How `environment` above was established, not just asserted. Provisional pending SP9's decision record — default `self_reported` until a corroboration mechanism lands; a `self_reported`-only environment claim is lower-weight evidence and S9 prose must say so, not silently treat it as confirmed.

assumptions.description: Data, access, dependency, rate/spend limit, notification-threshold, or reliability assumptions that affect readiness

release_evidence.description: Q2: What evidence shows the release is ready to move?

release_identifiers.description: The full identifier set for what is being released

health_and_smoke_evidence.description: Health check, smoke test, controlled failure/retry evidence refs

eval_coverage.description: Coverage by case class — the evidence unit is the class, not the test count

observability_plan.description: Q3: How will the team know what is happening after release?

key_signals.description: Most important health/availability/error/latency/usage/cost/quota signals, each naming the decision it supports

correlation_ids.description: Provider request IDs, client request IDs, rate-limit headers captured

sensitive_data_excluded.description: Named data classes that must not be logged

health_thresholds.description: docs/decisions/039: every signal that declared health_thresholds, rolled up per lens from the raw S4 design_fragments -- not deduplicated/merged across lenses, since S7's merge policy for a conflicting threshold set on the same attribute is an open question this report does not resolve. Omitted entirely when no fragment declared any.

thresholds.description: Verbatim copy of the signal's own health_thresholds (design_fragment.schema.json).

failure_response.description: Q4: What happens if the API fails or degrades?

failure_modes.description: Most important failure modes with their default response action

retry_degradation_fallback.description: Bounded retry policy, graceful-degradation behavior, fallback paths

recommendation.description: Q5: The release recommendation — the decision itself.

decision.description: ready: evidence present, no blocking gaps. ready_with_conditions: forward in a limited/controlled way under named, owned conditions tied to validation steps. remediate_before_release: blocking but fixable gaps must close before exposure. pause_and_redesign: the design itself is not fit for the workflow and needs substantial rework. escalate_for_review: risk exceeds the working team's authority — needs security/governance/platform/policy/customer decision. rollback_or_pause_expansion: post-release evidence says stop, pause, or return to a safer version.

evidence_that_would_change_decision.description: Directional falsifiability of the gate decision.

to_upgrade.description: What evidence would move the decision toward ready_with_conditions or ready (e.g. named source ownership, restricted-source exclusion, verified role/region path, expanded eval coverage, observability signals live, named support owner for a limited pilot)

to_escalate_or_downgrade.description: What would move it toward escalate_for_review or rollback (e.g. restricted-source, logging, privacy, or regional policy questions unresolvable at the working team's level)

s11_verdict_ref.description: Link to the technical validation verdict when S11 has run; the release recommendation is the decision layer above the technical verdict

evidence_position.description: Epistemic position of the recommendation — what is confirmed by evidence, what is assumed, and what remains unknown. Confidence, urgency, or a successful demo alone never move an item into 'confirmed'.

scope.description: Anti-scope-creep boundary: evidence-led, not ambition-led. Unsupported complexity added to a release is itself a risk that solves no blocker.

out_of_scope_unless_approved.description: Patterns that must not be silently added without separate workflow evidence and approvals (e.g. realtime/voice, multimodal, automated ticket creation, record updates, research-style synthesis)

data_and_governance.description: Security, data, and governance review — the release controls that make 'internal-only' insufficient as a risk argument.

input.description: What the API receives, incl. caller-asserted context and its verification status

output.description: What responses expose, incl. whether source approval/regional applicability is indicated

status.description: Approval status incl. regional/use-case scope, e.g. 'approved US/CA; UK pending'

pilot_handling.description: include / include for approved regions only / exclude / permission-gate and escalate

trust_boundary_verification.description: Which caller-asserted fields are verified server-side vs. trusted

tool_action_boundary.description: Declared external effects allowed in this release

governance_owners_unnamed.description: Decision areas (release approval, security signoff, source signoff, logging review, support) still lacking a named owner — each is a release blocker candidate

known_limitations.description: Handoff statement of what the product should NOT answer or do, and which regions, sources, roles, and cases remain limited. A handoff gap is as release-blocking as a technical gap: if nobody owns support, nobody owns the consequences.
